LanguageData.DynamicMending.OverclockDesc: Set how hard this machine runs, from 10% to 200%. Slower is more careful: at 10% it takes ten times as long but works like a skill 20 crafter, uses fewer materials and almost never botches a repair. At 100% and above it works like a skill 8 crafter (more with a better core); faster gets through gear quicker at no cost in skill. Power draw, heat and how often it breaks down all rise with the square of the speed, as power and heat do on Vanilla Furniture Expanded - Factory's machines, whose boosters and heatsinks also work on this one.

LanguageData.DynamicMending.CancelJobDesc: Stop the current job. The item, every material gathered for it, and anything waiting for a reject chute are put on the floor beside the machine. The item is forbidden so it is not brought straight back.

LanguageData.DynamicMending.BillOrderHint: The machine works down its bill list in order: the first bill whose filter takes an item decides what happens to it. A repair bill passes on gear it cannot repair (undamaged, above the auto-repair threshold) to the bills below it. Gear no bill takes goes out a reject chute.
LanguageData.DynamicMending.CoreUpgradeDesc: Give the machine a better brain. It runs on a {0} now. Each tier up adds +4 crafting skill (up to 20), works 20% faster and uses 20% fewer materials: standard subcore, high subcore, then a persona core. Pick one and a constructor brings it from storage and installs it; the core it replaces comes back out (the basic subcore it was built with stays part of the building). An upgraded core is returned when the machine is deconstructed.

LanguageData.DynamicMending.BillAllowComponentsDesc: Unticked, this bill skips gear whose repair would cost these (judged from the actual repair cost, after any core saving) and passes it on to the next bill - or out a reject chute if no bill takes it.
